newsitem.title: CHINA: China hails U.S. vote on MFN trade status.
newsitem.headline: China hails U.S. vote on MFN trade status.

text.p: China on Wednesday welcomed a decisive vote in the U.S. Congress that assured Beijing of Most Favoured Nation (MFN) trade status from Washington for another year.
A spokesman of the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation had welcomed the vote as in the interests of China and the United States, state television reported.
"Giving each other MFN treatment is a normal and mutually beneficial arrangement," the spokesman was quoted as saying.
"But it should be pointed out the United States until now still insists on annual review of China's MFN treatment in accordance with its domestic laws.

"We hope the U.S. side could take measures as early as possible to change this kind of abnormal practice and permanently resolve China's MFN treatment to ensure stable and smooth development of economic and trade ties between the two countries," the spokesman said.
The U.S. House of Representatives voted by a sizeable margin of 259 to 173 to renew China's Most Favoured Nation status, backing President Bill Clinton's decision in May.
